claim.pdf_says: Format 2 (reporting):  USE [ GLOBAL ] BEFORE REPORTING identifier-1  — USE, GLOBAL, BEFORE and REPORTING are all underlined (required words); only identifier-1 is not.
claim.markdown_says:
Format 2 (reporting):

USE [ GLOBAL ] BEFORE REPORTING identifier-1   (ISO_COBOL.md line 32562 — bare prose, no code fence, and no 'Figure notes' paragraph, unlike Formats 1, 3 and 4 on the same page which each carry one)
claim.why_it_matters: Formats 1, 3 and 4 on this page each record which words are underlined in a Figure-notes paragraph; Format 2 records nothing, so the required-word marking on BEFORE and REPORTING is simply absent. A reader or generator applying the page's own convention would infer that no word in Format 2 is required, i.e. that 'USE REPORTING identifier-1' or 'USE BEFORE identifier-1' is legal.

verdict.reasoning: Both sides of the claim check out against the primary sources, and the lost item is normative meta-language rather than styling. (1) PDF, rendered at 300 dpi and cropped on the Format 2 line (E:/Temp/specrecon/v804/fmt2.png): I read the printed glyphs directly and see four separate underline rules — one under USE, one under GLOBAL, one under BEFORE, one under REPORTING. The square brackets around GLOBAL and the word identifier-1 carry no rule. So the claimed PDF reading is exact. (2) Markdown, specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 32562: the line is literally 'USE [ GLOBAL ] BEFORE REPORTING identifier-1' — unfenced, with no <u> markup and no following '> **Figure notes ...**' paragraph. Formats 1, 3 and 4 on the same page (page-804.md lines 35, 49, 59) each do carry a Figure-notes paragraph enumerating their underlined words. So the claimed markdown reading is exact as well. (3) The loss is semantic, not cosmetic formatting. ISO_COBOL.md line 2628 (clause 5.2, Keywords) states keywords 'are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats' and 'are required'; line 2641 states optional words 'are shown in uppercase and not underlined' and merely 'may be written to add clarity'. Under the standard's own convention an unmarked uppercase word in a general format is an omittable optional word, so a mechanical reader of line 32562 would conclude BEFORE and REPORTING are noise words. Nowhere else does the markdown record their requiredness: the syntax and general rules (lines 32620-32624, 32725-32737) only use the phrase 'USE BEFORE REPORTING' in prose, which is inference rather than the meta-language marking. (4) I checked the counter-argument that unfenced one-line formats simply never carry underline information in this transcription; it fails. A survey of all 147 'General format:' / 'Format N (...):' headers shows the file preserves underlining for short one-line formats with inline <u>...</u> markup — e.g. line 12927 '<u>FUNCTION-ID</u>. user-function-name-1 [ <u>AS</u> literal-1 ] **.**', line 14782 '<u>SELECT</u> [ <u>OPTIONAL</u> ] file-name-1', line 15741 '<u>SAME</u> <u>RECORD</u> AREA FOR file-name-1 { file-name-2 } …'. Page 804's Format 2 uses neither available mechanism. This is therefore a genuine content omission, not page furniture, wrapping, or a style choice.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but the claim under-states the scope and over-states one inference. What is actually missing is ALL FOUR required-word markers, not just two: the PDF underlines USE, GLOBAL, BEFORE and REPORTING (four discrete rules, verified glyph-by-glyph on the 300 dpi crop), and ISO_COBOL.md line 32562 records none of them. The full statement text is present and correctly ordered, and the optionality of GLOBAL survives via the brackets; the only thing lost is the keyword/optional-word distinction, whose loss reads under clause 5.2 (ISO_COBOL.md lines 2628 and 2641) as making BEFORE and REPORTING omittable optional words. Two corrections to the claim's framing: (a) 'no code fence' is not itself a defect — 57 of the 147 general-format headers in the file are transcribed unfenced, which is the file's normal treatment of short one-line formats; the defect is solely the absent underline marking. (b) The remedy is not necessarily a Figure-notes paragraph: the file's established convention for unfenced one-liners is inline <u>...</u>, so the correct repair is 'USE [ <u>GLOBAL</u> ] <u>BEFORE</u> <u>REPORTING</u> identifier-1' with <u>USE</u>, matching e.g. line 14782. Finally, this is not isolated to page 804 — the same omission exists at least at lines 14821 and 14878 (SELECT clause Formats 3 (sequential) and 4 (sort-merge), transcribed as bare 'SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1' while the sibling Format 2 at line 14782 carries the <u> markup), so it should be fixed as a pattern sweep over unfenced one-line general formats rather than as a one-page edit. Severity 'cosmetic' is defensible for reading but understated for machine consumption: a grammar generator driven off the markdown would emit BEFORE and REPORTING as optional noise words.
